subject: Banking
title: QR Code Payments in China
description: A 60-second lesson on QR Code Payments in China.

hook.text: In China, street food vendors display QR codes. Customers scan, pay, and walk away. Cash barely exists in daily life.

buildup.text: Alipay and WeChat Pay dominate with over 1.5 billion combined users.

discovery.text: QR payments are cheap. No card terminal needed. A printed piece of paper with a code becomes a payment acceptance.

twist.text: The Chinese government worries about Alipay and WeChat's power. Two companies control most of the nation's payment data.

climax.text: QR payments show that the cheapest infrastructure wins. A printed code beats a $500 card terminal.

punchline.text: A printed QR code replaces card terminals. China went mobile-first.

quiz.question: Why did QR code payments dominate in China over card networks?
options: QR codes need no expensive merchant terminal hardware

details.summary: QR code payments through Alipay and WeChat Pay dominate Chinese commerce, where scanning a code replaces cash and cards for everything from street food to luxury purchases, processing over 100 trillion yuan annually.
details.whyItMatters: China leapfrogged credit cards entirely, moving from cash directly to mobile payments. This model shows how different payment cultures can develop based on local conditions rather than following Western patterns.
takeaways: Alipay and WeChat Pay process over 100 trillion yuan annually
QR codes replaced the need for expensive card terminal infrastructure
Street vendors and taxi drivers accept QR payments universally

faq.question: Why did QR payments succeed in China but not the West?
faq.answer: China had low credit card penetration, making QR codes a leap from cash. Western countries already had mature card infrastructure. Also, Alipay and WeChat are super-apps with built-in payment, while Western equivalents are fragmented.

faq.question: Are QR code payments secure?
faq.answer: Reasonably so. Dynamic QR codes change with each transaction. However, scams involving fake QR codes placed over legitimate ones have occurred. The systems use fraud detection but rely heavily on trust in the platform ecosystem.
